items.title: From field to fragrance: A review on post-harvest technologies and value addition in jasmine
items.summary: Jasmine (Jasminum spp.) is a valuable flower crop grown widely in tropical and subtropical regions for its cultural, ornamental and industrial importance. However, its high perishability, rapid aging and loss of fragrance create significant challenges for post-harvest handling, marketability and export potential. This review brings together current knowledge on the post-harvest biology of jasmine flowers. It focuses on key biochemical changes, including membrane damage, oxidative stress, enzymatic browning and the timing of the pathways that produce fragrance. items.title: Microbial volatile humulene orchestrates plant–microbe alliance to establish disease‐suppressive rhizosphere
items.summary: Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) suppress growth and virulence traits of soil-borne pathogens, yet their ecological roles in disease suppression remain unclear. items.summary: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. items.summary: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a refractory complication of antiresorptive and antiangiogenic therapies. From an osteoimmunological perspective, this review proposes that MRONJ may be more accurately understood as an immune-mediated failure of healing within a jaw-specific osteoimmune niche, in which pathological macrophage reprogramming arises from the interplay between pharmacological exposure and the local microenvironment. items.title: Epigenetic and RNA-mediated regulation of plant VOC biosynthesis and signalling
items.summary: Plants use volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as airborne signals in development, defence, and ecological interactions. Epigenetic mechanisms can influence VOC biosynthesis and, in some experimental systems, plant responses to volatile cues. This review examines chromatin-level mechanisms, particularly DNA methylation and histone modifications, in VOC biosynthesis and responses to volatile cues, together with distinct RNA-level regulation by non-coding RNAs and m 6 A-dependent epitranscriptomic mechanisms. items.source: Biomedical Journal of Scientific & Technical Research
items.summary: Squalene is a strategically important pharmaceutical lipid used in established oil-in-water vaccine adjuvants and increasingly investigated in nanomedicine. items.title: Structural basis of mevalonate pathway regulation by feedback inhibition of mevalonate kinase
items.summary: The mevalonate pathway diverts acetyl-CoA from central metabolism to produce isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP) and dimethylallyl pyrophosphate (DMAPP), the universal precursors to all steroids and isoprenoids in biology. Mevalonate kinase (MK) catalyzes a key regulatory step of mevalonate pathway in many eukaryotes, in which several downstream isoprenoid pyrophosphates act as feedback inhibitors. Known MK inhibitors vary widely in size, including IPP and DMAPP (five carbons, C 5 ), geranyl pyrophosphate (GPP, C 10 ), farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP, C 15 ), and geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP, C 20 ).
